en: The Jātaka:
The Eighth Chapter,
the Section on Kaccāyana.
1. The Kaccāni Jātaka:
“Clad in white garments, with pure and wet hair, Kaccāni, why do you sit leaning against a water-jar?”
“You are washing flour, sesame seeds, and rice grains;
for what reason will there be sesame-rice?
“O Brahmin, this is not for the sake of food.”
"Tilodana will be well-cooked;
today the Dhamma is considered by him to be abundant,
and I shall perform [the rites] in the midst of the charnel ground."
“Having investigated, Kaccāna, perform what is to be done.
What Dhamma has been taught by you alone?
[He is] the Thousand-Eyed One of incomparable power.”
“The excellent Dhamma never dies.
“O Brahmā, my firm conviction in this is that the Dhamma is dead; I have no doubt about this.”
Those who were indeed wicked have now become happy;
for my daughter-in-law was once barren.
Having killed me, she gave birth to her son;
now she is the mistress of the entire family,
while I am cast out here all alone.
“I live, indeed, I am not dead;
I have come here for your very sake.
She who, having killed you, gave birth to a son—”
“Together with my son, I shall turn myself to ashes.
“If this is what pleases you, O King of Gods,
then you have come here for my very sake.”
“I, my son, my daughter-in-law, and my grandson—
may we dwell together in our home in mutual harmony.
“If this is what pleases you, Kātiyāni,” [he replied].
Even though you have been struck down, do not abandon the Dhamma;
you, your son, your daughter-in-law, and your grandson—
may you all dwell together in the home in harmony.
That Kātiyānī lived in her home in harmony with her daughter-in-law;
her son and grandson waited upon her.
“...was taken possession of by Devānaminda.
Thus ends the first Kaccāni Jātaka.
